newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P says cuts ratings of Nikko Sec and Daiwa Sec.
newsitem.headline: S&P says cuts ratings of Nikko Sec and Daiwa Sec.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) announced on Wednesday that it had lowered the long- and short-term debt and counterparty ratings of Nikko Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
The firms are among the nation's "Big Four" brokerages.

The latest cut in the two firms' ratings reflects the prolonged poor performance of Japanese securities firms and the expected negative impact of ongoing deregulation, especially the liberalisation of stock brokerage commissions, S&P said.

A recovery in securities firms has been delayed due to unstable stock market conditions, heightening competition, narrowing margins and inflexible cost structures. Most companies have posted losses or low profits over the past six years.

As a result of large losses in 1996/97 resulting from falling stock prices, the firms' capital adequacy will further decline, which might constrain each participant's business expansion plans, S&P said.

Nikko has tried to diversify its revenue base, but its reliance on stock brokerage commissions is slightly higher than that of Nomura Securities Co Ltd and Daiwa, which makes Nikko's performance more vulnerable to market conditions.

Any Nikko cost-saving efforts would be partly offset by increased investment costs for new products and systems, S&P said. Nikko's credit quality, nevertheless, is sustained by its adequate capital ratio and good product-development capability and distribution, the agency added.

Daiwa, meanwhile, has not been very successful in increasing its revenues or in curtailing operating costs, it said. Daiwa is likely to remain a major player in the Japanese capital market, due to its wide customer base and the current huge gap between the Big Four securities firms and their smaller peers in the domestic market.
It said the ratings outlook was stable, adding that both Nikko and Daiwa would be able to sustain the new ratings while dealing with Japan's ongoing financial deregulation.
S&P said it had also lowered ratings on the two firms' related entities such as Nikko Europe Plc and Daiwa Europe Ltd.
